name: Button
summary: A button is a control that does something on the current page. The native <button> element already carries the role, the tab stop, Enter and Space, and its accessible name, so there is no ARIA to add. The hard part is everything around it: the missing type attribute, and choosing between disabled and aria-disabled.
demoNote: Every example under Common mistakes is live, so you can press each one and watch it fail. Tab through example 4 and you get two stops for three controls.

contract.useWhen: A real button, plus why a div with a click handler is not one.
keyboard: native: moves to and from the button. disabled removes the stop, aria-disabled keeps it
activates. Native to <button>; a div owes both by hand
failureModes: no type attribute, so a button inside a form is a submit button
a div with a click handler: no role, no keys, no focus, and nothing for voice input
disabled when the person needs to know why — it is unfocusable and announces nothing
